P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Under the BCC's 2014 exchange regulation, service exporters are not required to surrender their export receipts to banks or the BCC (art. 33). The 60-day repatriation deadline in art. 32 is written for goods exports. Règlement 001/25 (16 Apr 2025) added a ban on carrying USD 10,000 or more in cash between towns where banks exist (bank transfer required); it does not change the receipts rules.

sources.publisher: Banque Centrale du Congo — Réglementation du change (2014) (copy on droitcongolais.info)
sources.title: Réglementation du change, art. 33 al. 3
sources.quote: Alinéa 3 : Les exportateurs des services ne sont pas tenus de rétrocéde r leurs recettes d’exportation aux banques ou à la Banque Centrale du Congo.

sources.publisher: Banque Centrale du Congo — Règlement n° 001/25 (16 Apr 2025)
sources.title: Règlement n° 001/25 modifiant et complétant la Réglementation du change du 28 mars 2014, art. 1
sources.quote: avec une somme en espèce égale ou supérieure à 10.000 dollars américains ou son équivalent en d'autres monnaies étrangères. Les sommes excédant ce plafond doivent faire l'objet d'un transfert bancaire.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: 2014 text read from a droitcongolais.info copy (OCR-like spacing kept, e.g. 'rétrocéde r'); BCC dates the regulation 28 March 2014. Règlement 001/25 is an image-only scan (pages rendered and read); it repeals Règlement 003/18. Whether other amendments touched arts. 32/33/73 not checked. Press reports a ban on cash FX transactions from April 2027 (unverified).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Approved banks may open foreign-currency accounts for residents (RME) and non-residents without prior BCC authorisation, and these accounts can be credited and debited freely (art. 73).

sources.publisher: Banque Centrale du Congo — Réglementation du change (2014) (copy on droitcongolais.info)
sources.title: Réglementation du change, art. 73
sources.quote: Article 73 : Alinéa 1 : Les banques agréées sont autorisées à ouvrir des comptes en monnaies étrangères au profit des résidents (RME) et non -résidents (NRME) sans autorisation préalable de la Banque Centrale du Congo.

P2_fcy_account.notes: The economy is heavily dollarised; USD accounts are common.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Democratic Republic of the Congo (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program. Restricted: Paddle lists it as an unsupported seller country; Lemon Squeezy blocks buyers there.

P3_local_gateways.notes: Not established. Mobile money (M-Pesa, Orange Money, Airtel Money) is widespread; no gateway onboarding individuals for online acceptance was sourced.

P4_paypal.answer: Unclear. 'Congo - Kinshasa' is listed as a PayPal market but is not on the PayPal Payouts list; no reliable source on withdrawals was found.

P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Wise: the DRC is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money. Payoneer: not confirmed.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Registration goes through the GUCE (Guichet Unique de Création d'Entreprise, Decree 14/014 of 8 May 2014). It bundles the RCCM, national identification number, tax number and social-security affiliation, with a legal limit of three working days for a complete file. Real-world cost and time are disputed: the World Bank's B-READY 2024 found up to 85 days and USD 1,700 in official fees, while GUCE says fees are USD 110 for an SARL. Individual-enterprise fees were not confirmed officially.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The 'numéro impôt' (tax number, instituted by Decree 03/012 of 2003), assigned by the DGI delegate at the GUCE during business creation, alongside the RCCM.

sources.quote: La RDC, membre de l'OHADA, délivre le RCCM et le numéro impôt en un seul dossier centralisé.

L2_tax_id.notes: OCR text ('numéto impôr'); procedure for individuals outside GUCE not sourced.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Since 1 January 2026, Law 23/053 of 30 Nov 2023 replaced the old schedular system with corporate tax (IS) and personal income tax (IRPP). Residents are now taxed on worldwide income, including services performed for foreign clients; previously only Congolese-source income was taxable. Per the DGI presentation, micro-enterprises (turnover under CDF 25m) pay a flat USD 30, and small enterprises (CDF 25m–300m) pay 1% of turnover for sales of goods or 2% for services.

sources.title: L'imposition des revenus de sources étrangères des personnes physiques résidentes en droit fiscal congolais (30 May 2026)
sources.quote: Entrée en vigueur le 1er janvier 2026, elle institue un impôt global sur le revenu des personnes physiques fondé sur le critère de la résidence, conduisant à soumettre à l'imposition congolaise l'intégralité des revenus du résident, quelle qu'en soit l'origine géographique.

sources.quote: le principe de la territorialité mondiale pour les résidents et de la territorialité différenciée pour les non-résidents pour l’IRPP ;

PwC's corporate page already shows 25m/300m. Law text itself (art. 58/59) not read.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT 16%, a reduced rate on specific essential goods, and 0% on exports and assimilated transactions (PwC). Persons become liable from annual turnover of CDF 80m (Légavox; the 2010 ordinance-law said 50m, raised by a 2011 ministerial order per secondary sources). A taxpayer who falls below the threshold stays registered for two years. Whether exported services count as 0%-rated exports was not confirmed.

sources.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: There are three rates: A standard rate of 16%.

sources.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: A rate of 0% on exports and assimilated transactions.

sources.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: A reduced rate of 1% applies to specific essential goods

sources.title: Théorie et pratique de la TVA en R.D. Congo
sources.quote: En effet, les personnes physiques ou morales sont assujetties à la TVA lorsqu’elles réalisent un chiffre d’affaires annuel égal ou supérieur à 80.000.000 de francs congolais .

L4_vat_gst.notes: Threshold from one secondary domain; not checked against a 2026 official text. Interaction of the CDF 80m VAT threshold with the new 25m/300m small-enterprise bands not established. A blog says liberal professions are VAT-liable regardless of turnover (not verified).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Digital Code (Ordonnance-loi 23/010 of 13 Mar 2023) governs personal data. Processing requires prior declaration to the Data Protection Authority (APD, art. 186). The APD has not yet been set up; its powers are exercised provisionally by the telecom regulator ARPTC, which on 11 Sep 2025 issued a decision on declaration and authorisation procedures (including fees). Commentators argue that decision is unlawful.

sources.publisher: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code du numérique (text on droitnumerique.cd)
sources.title: Code du numérique, art. 186
sources.quote: Le traitement des données personnelles est soumis à une déclaration préalable auprès de l’Autorité de protection des données.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Digital Code, consumers (B2C only) may withdraw within 72 hours, without reasons and bearing only direct return costs (art. 62). The period becomes 15 days if the seller failed its pre-contract information duty. The seller must refund within 72 hours of the withdrawal notice. For services already started, the client pays pro rata for what was delivered.

sources.quote: Nonobstant l’accord entre les parties, avant le jour de l’expédition prévu dans le contrat, le client dispose d’un délai de soixante-douze (72) heures pour exercer son droit de rétractation.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: No freelancer-specific incentive was found. The flat USD 30 micro-enterprise regime (turnover under CDF 25m, L3) is the main simplification.
L7_incentives.note: No incentive source found on 2026-10-22; micro regime covered in L3.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: There has been no national ID card since 1997. The voter card issued by CENI serves as the ID card and may be required for banking transactions, though each card is tied to one electoral cycle.
D1_id_document.note: Single source (Canada IRB country research, Apr 2024); bank/BCC KYC rules not captured on 2026-10-22.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
